title: Elasticity feedback loop causing reserved-pool shortfall for burst traffic
creator: Marco Ortega
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported transient 503s and degraded throughput during afternoon traffic spikes on dedicated pools. Root cause traced to an emergent feedback loop between the reserved-pool allocator and the autoscaler: pre-warm requests were being counted as queued reservations before slots were fully warming, which suppressed further scale-up signals until burst credits were exhausted. The net effect was a shortfall in available warmed slots during burst windows, causing requests to fall back to lower-capacity variants or fail.
root_cause: The autoscaler used a heuristic that inferred headroom from pending reservation messages in the allocator queue. When warmup latencies increased (due to kernel contention on some nodes), those queued reservations persisted and were interpreted as 'in-progress allocations', preventing additional scale-ups. Simultaneously, the burst-credit accounting service did not account for deferred warmups, accelerating credit depletion and preventing burst recovery. A race in the slot confirmation path allowed the allocator to mark slots as assigned before KV cache preflight finished, producing false-positive capacity signals.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated reserved pool with burst enabled and low baseline headroom (2-4 slots).
2) Generate a sudden multi-tenant spike aligned to the pool's warmup profile (500ms+ node init).
3) Instrument autoscaler metrics: scale_up_signals, allocator_pending_reservations, slot_confirmations, burst_credit_balance.
4) Observe pending_reservations stay high while scale_up_signals are suppressed and burst_credit_balance drops until requests begin failing or fallback to lower-tier models.
mitigations: Hotfix deployed to require explicit slot_confirmed telemetry from node before counting it as allocated (patch: autoscaler/allocator: require preflight_confirm).
Temporarily increased warmup headroom for affected dedicated pools via control-plane override (customer-facing mitigation).
Enabled conservative burst fallback policy for 24h window to protect SLA-exposed tenants while fix rolled out.
Revived emergency runbook step to drain pending reservations and force scale-up when queued reservation age > 5s.
resolution: Merged autoscaler patch that: (a) treats queued reservations as provisional until node preflight_confirm is received, (b) introduces a 7s 'allocation-timeout' after which autoscaler will force an additional scale-up, and (c) delays burst-credit debit until preflight_confirm to avoid premature credit consumption. Canary rolled to us-west-2 for 6h, then global rollout. Customer 1 and Customer 2 verified no further 503s during subsequent peak windows. Rollback safe-path validated.
postmortem_actions: Add integration test that simulates delayed node preflight and verifies autoscaler still performs corrective scale-ups.
Add metric: allocator.pending_provisional_count and alert when > threshold for >30s.
Run a 2-week campaign to increase default reserved-pool headroom recommendations in provisioning templates for new customers.
Schedule follow-up to audit burst-credit accounting to ensure alignment with actual allocation lifecycle.
